sanskrit: rāghavaś cāpi vipulaṃ taṃ rākṣasavanaukasām śrutvā saṃgrāmanirghoṣaṃ jāmbavantam uvāca ha
english: Rāghava too, upon hearing that vast tumult of battle from the forest-dwelling rākṣasas, then spoke to Jāmbavān.

sanskrit: saumya nūnaṃ hanumatā kṛtaṃ karma suduṣkaram śrūyate hi yathā bhīmaḥ sumahān āyudhasvanaḥ
english: "Surely, gentle one, Hanumān has performed a deed most difficult to accomplish, for that fearful, immense clash of weapons is heard even here.

sanskrit: tad gaccha kuru sāhāyyaṃ svabalenābhisaṃvṛtaḥ kṣipram ṛṣkapate tasya kapiśreṣṭhasya yudhyataḥ
english: Therefore go, lord of bears, surrounded by your own army, and render swift aid to that foremost of monkeys while he fights."

sanskrit: ṛkṣarājas tathety uktvā svenānīkena saṃvṛtaḥ āgacchat paścimadvāraṃ hanūmān yatra vānaraḥ
english: The king of bears, saying "so be it," surrounded by his own forces, went to the western gate where the monkey Hanumān was.

sanskrit: athāyāntaṃ hanūmantaṃ dadarśarkṣapatiḥ pathi vānaraiḥ kṛtasaṃgrāmaiḥ śvasadbhir abhisaṃvṛtam
english: Then the lord of bears saw, on the road, Hanumān coming, surrounded by monkeys who had been fighting and were now panting with exhaustion.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā pathi hanūmāṃś ca tad ṛṣkabalam udyatam nīlameghanibhaṃ bhīmaṃ saṃnivārya nyavartata
english: Seeing on the road both Hanumān and that upraised bear-army, dark as a rain-cloud and fearsome, he checked his advance and turned back.

sanskrit: sa tena harisainyena saṃnikarṣaṃ mahāyaśāḥ śīghram āgamya rāmāya duḥkhito vākyam abravīt
english: He of great renown, having quickly come into the presence of that monkey-army, spoke these words to Rāma in grief:

sanskrit: samare yudhyamānānām asmākaṃ prekṣatāṃ ca saḥ jaghāna rudatīṃ sītām indrajid rāvaṇātmajaḥ
english: "Even as we were fighting in battle and looking on, Indrajit, son of Rāvaṇa, slew Sītā who was weeping."

sanskrit: udbhrāntacittas tāṃ dṛṣṭvā viṣaṇṇo 'ham ariṃdama tad ahaṃ bhavato vṛttaṃ vijñāpayitum āgataḥ
english: "Seeing her, O subduer of foes, my mind was overcome with agitation and I fell into despair; therefore I have come to inform you of this event."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rāghavaḥ śokamūrchitaḥ nipapāta tadā bhūmau chinnamūla iva drumaḥ
english: Hearing those words of his, Rāghava fainted with grief and fell then to the ground like a tree whose roots have been severed.

sanskrit: taṃ bhūmau devasaṃkāśaṃ patitaṃ dṛśya rāghavam abhipetuḥ samutpatya sarvataḥ kapisattamāḥ
english: Seeing Rāghava, resplendent as a god, fallen upon the ground, the foremost monkeys leaped forward and rushed to him from all sides.

sanskrit: asiñcan salilaiś cainaṃ padmotpalasugandhibhiḥ pradahantam asahyaṃ ca sahasāgnim ivotthitam
english: They sprinkled him with water fragrant with lotuses and blue water-lilies, as he blazed with an unbearable anguish, suddenly arisen like fire.

sanskrit: taṃ lakṣmaṇo 'tha bāhubhyāṃ pariṣvajya suduḥkhitaḥ uvāca rāmam asvasthaṃ vākyaṃ hetvarthasaṃhitam
english: Then Lakṣmaṇa, deeply grieved, embraced him with both arms and spoke to the unwell Rāma words full of reason and import:

sanskrit: śubhe vartmani tiṣṭhantaṃ tvām āryavijitendriyam anarthebhyo na śaknoti trātuṃ dharmo nirarthakaḥ
english: "You who walk on the auspicious path and have mastered your senses like a noble man — dharma that is ineffectual cannot protect you from misfortunes.

sanskrit: bhūtānāṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ ca jaṅgamānāṃ ca darśanam yathāsti na tathā dharmas tena nāstīti me matiḥ
english: "The existence of beings, both stationary and moving, is plainly perceived; but dharma is not so manifest — therefore in my view it does not exist.

sanskrit: yathaiva sthāvaraṃ vyaktaṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca tathāvidham nāyam arthas tathā yuktas tvadvidho na vipadyate
english: "Just as the stationary and the moving are plainly seen, this matter is not equally apt — for one such as you should not meet with calamity.

sanskrit: yady adharmo bhaved bhūto rāvaṇo narakaṃ vrajet bhavāṃś ca dharmasaṃyukto naivaṃ vyasanam āpnuyāt
english: "If adharma were truly existent, Rāvaṇa would go to hell; and you, endowed with dharma, would not thus suffer this misfortune.

sanskrit: tasya ca vyasanābhāvād vyasanaṃ ca gate tvayi dharmeṇopalabhed dharmam adharmaṃ cāpy adharmataḥ
english: "But since he knows no affliction while affliction has come to you, one must conclude from dharma that there is dharma and from adharma, adharma.

sanskrit: yadi dharmeṇa yujyeran nādharmarucayo janāḥ dharmeṇa caratāṃ dharmas tathā caiṣāṃ phalaṃ bhavet
english: "If those who delight in adharma were bound by dharma, then dharma would indeed come to those who practise dharma, and such would be their fruit.

sanskrit: yasmād arthā vivardhante yeṣv adharmaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ kliśyante dharmaśīlāś ca tasmād etau nirarthakau
english: "Since wealth increases in those in whom adharma is established, while those of virtuous conduct are afflicted, both dharma and adharma are therefore without purpose.

sanskrit: vadhyante pāpakarmāṇo yady adharmeṇa rāghava vadhakarmahato dharmaḥ sa hataḥ kaṃ vadhiṣyati
english: "If evildoers are slain by adharma, O Rāghava, then dharma, itself slain by the act of slaying, is destroyed — whom then can it slay?

sanskrit: atha vā vihitenāyaṃ hanyate hanti vā param vidhir ālipyate tena na sa pāpena karmaṇā
english: "Or if he is slain or slays another by divine ordinance, then fate is implicated in it and is not tainted by that sinful act.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭapratikāreṇa avyaktenāsatā satā kathaṃ śakyaṃ paraṃ prāptuṃ dharmeṇārivikarśana
english: "With dharma that is unseen in its recompense, unmanifest, both real and unreal — how, O crusher of enemies, can the highest be attained through it?

sanskrit: yadi sat syāt satāṃ mukhya nāsat syāt tava kiṃ cana tvayā yadīdṛśaṃ prāptaṃ tasmāt san nopapadyate
english: "If the real existed, O foremost of the righteous, nothing unreal would touch you; since you have met with such a thing, the real therefore does not hold.

sanskrit: atha vā durbalaḥ klībo balaṃ dharmo 'nuvartate durbalo hṛtamaryādo na sevya iti me matiḥ
english: "Or perhaps dharma is feeble and impotent, following in the wake of strength; the feeble, with its dignity stripped away, is not to be served — such is my view.

sanskrit: balasya yadi ced dharmo guṇabhūtaḥ parākrame dharmam utsṛjya vartasva yathā dharme tathā bale
english: "If dharma is but an attribute of strength and valour, then abandon dharma and act — in strength as in dharma.

sanskrit: atha cet satyavacanaṃ dharmaḥ kila paraṃtapa anṛtas tvayy akaruṇaḥ kiṃ na baddhas tvayā pitā
english: "If dharma is indeed truthfulness in speech, O scorcher of enemies, then why did you not restrain your father when he was cruel and untrue to you?

sanskrit: yadi dharmo bhaved bhūta adharmo vā paraṃtapa na sma hatvā muniṃ vajrī kuryād ijyāṃ śatakratuḥ
english: "If dharma truly existed, O scorcher of foes, or adharma — Vajrī who wields the thunderbolt would not have performed the hundred-sacrifice after slaying a sage.

sanskrit: adharmasaṃśrito dharmo vināśayati rāghava sarvam etad yathākāmaṃ kākutstha kurute naraḥ
english: "Dharma rooted in adharma destroys, O Rāghava; all this, O Kākutstha, a man does as he pleases.

sanskrit: mama cedaṃ mataṃ tāta dharmo 'yam iti rāghava dharmamūlaṃ tvayā chinnaṃ rājyam utsṛjatā tadā
english: "Such is my view, dear one — this is dharma — O Rāghava, when you renounced the kingdom you severed the very root of dharma.

sanskrit: arthebhyo hi vivṛddhebhyaḥ saṃvṛddhebhyas tatas tataḥ kriyāḥ sarvāḥ pravartante parvatebhya ivāpagāḥ
english: "For from wealth that grows and multiplies on all sides, all undertakings proceed, as rivers flow from mountains.

sanskrit: arthena hi viyuktasya puruṣasyālpatejasaḥ vyucchidyante kriyāḥ sarvā grīṣme kusarito yathā
english: "For the man bereft of wealth, whose energy is slight, all his undertakings are cut off, as a stream dries in summer.

sanskrit: so 'yam arthaṃ parityajya sukhakāmaḥ sukhaidhitaḥ pāpam ārabhate kartuṃ tathā doṣaḥ pravartate
english: "Thus he who, desiring pleasure and having been raised in comfort, abandons wealth, begins to do evil — and so fault sets in.

sanskrit: yasyārthās tasya mitrāṇi yasyārthās tasya bāndhavaḥ yasyārthāḥ sa pumāṃl loke yasyārthāḥ sa ca paṇḍitaḥ
english: "He who has wealth has friends; he who has wealth has kinsmen; he who has wealth is a man in this world; he who has wealth is the learned one.

sanskrit: yasyārthāḥ sa ca vikrānto yasyārthāḥ sa ca buddhimān yasyārthāḥ sa mahābhāgo yasyārthāḥ sa mahāguṇaḥ
english: "He who has wealth is the heroic one; he who has wealth is the wise one; he who has wealth is the greatly fortunate; he who has wealth possesses great virtues.

sanskrit: arthasyaite parityāge doṣāḥ pravyāhṛtā mayā rājyam utsṛjatā vīra yena buddhis tvayā kṛtā
english: "These faults of abandoning wealth have been declared by me — O hero, it was with such reasoning that you resolved to renounce the kingdom.

sanskrit: yasyārthā dharmakāmārthās tasya sarvaṃ pradakṣiṇam adhanenārthakāmane nārthaḥ śakyo vicinvatā
english: "For him who has wealth, dharma, desire, and wealth all revolve auspiciously around him; for one who is without wealth and yet seeks wealth, wealth cannot be gathered.

sanskrit: harṣaḥ kāmaś ca darpaś ca dharmaḥ krodhaḥ śamo damaḥ arthād etāni sarvāṇi pravartante narādhipa
english: "Joy, desire, pride, dharma, anger, tranquillity, self-restraint — all these, O lord of men, proceed from wealth.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ naśyaty ayaṃ lokaś caratāṃ dharmacāriṇām te 'rthās tvayi na dṛśyante durdineṣu yathā grahāḥ
english: "For those who walk in dharma's path, this world perishes — those resources are not visible in you, as planets are invisible on stormy days.

sanskrit: tvayi pravrajite vīra guroś ca vacane sthite rakṣasāpahṛtā bhāryā prāṇaiḥ priyatarā tava
english: "O hero, when you went into exile and abided by your father's word, your wife — dearer to you than life — was carried off by a rākṣasa.

sanskrit: tad adya vipulaṃ vīra duḥkham indrajitā kṛtam karmaṇā vyapaneṣyāmi tasmād uttiṣṭha rāghava
english: "Therefore today, O hero, I shall remove by my deeds this great sorrow caused by Indrajit — so arise, O Rāghava.

sanskrit: ayam anagha tavoditaḥ priyārthaṃ janakasutā nidhanaṃ nirīkṣya ruṣṭaḥ sahayagajarathāṃ sarākṣasendrāṃ bhṛśam iṣubhir vinipātayāmi laṅkām
english: "O sinless one, enraged for your sake, having witnessed the slaying of Janaka's daughter, I shall fiercely pierce Laṅkā with arrows — together with its cavalry, elephants, chariots, and all the rākṣasa lords."

sanskrit: rāmam āśvāsayāne tu lakṣmaṇe bhrātṛvatsale svasthāne nikṣipya gulmān tatrāgacchad vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: While Lakṣmaṇa, devoted to his brother, was thus consoling Rāma, having posted sentinels at their proper stations, Vibhīṣaṇa arrived there.

sanskrit: nānāpraharaṇair vīraiś caturbhiḥ sacivair vṛtaḥ nīlāñjanacayākārair mātaṃgair iva yūthapaḥ
english: He was attended by four counsellors, heroes armed with diverse weapons, resembling the bull-leader of a herd of elephants dark as a mass of collyrium.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya mahātmānaṃ rāghavaṃ śokalālasaṃ vānarāṃś caiva dadṛśe bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇān
english: Approaching, he saw the great-souled Rāghava languishing in sorrow, and the monkeys too with eyes clouded by tears.

sanskrit: rāghavaṃ ca mahātmānam ikṣvākukulanandanam dadarśa moham āpannaṃ lakṣmaṇasyāṅkam āśritam
english: He saw the great-souled Rāghava, delight of the Ikṣvāku lineage, overcome by bewilderment and resting in Lakṣmaṇa's lap.

sanskrit: vrīḍitaṃ śokasaṃtaptaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ antarduḥkhena dīnātmā kim etad iti so 'bravīt
english: Seeing Rāma ashamed and tormented by sorrow, Vibhīṣaṇa, his spirit dejected with inner pain, said, "What is this?"

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇa mukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā sugrīvaṃ tāṃś ca vānarān uvāca lakṣmaṇo vākyam idaṃ bāṣpapariplutaḥ
english: Seeing Vibhīṣaṇa's face and Sugrīva and those monkeys, Lakṣmaṇa spoke these words, his voice choked with tears:

sanskrit: hatām indrajitā sītām iha śrutvaiva rāghavaḥ hanūmad vacanāt saumya tato moham upāgataḥ
english: "Hearing, gentle one, from Hanumān's report that Sītā had been slain by Indrajit, Rāghava straightway fell into a swoon."

sanskrit: kathayantaṃ tu saumitriṃ saṃnivārya vibhīṣaṇaḥ puṣkalārtham idaṃ vākyaṃ visaṃjñaṃ rāmam abravīt
english: Restraining Saumitri as he was speaking, Vibhīṣaṇa spoke these words of weighty import to the unconscious Rāma:

sanskrit: manujendrārtarūpeṇa yad uktas tvaṃ hanūmatā tad ayuktam ahaṃ manye sāgarasyeva śoṣaṇam
english: "What has been told to you by Hanumān in the form of news fit for a lord of men — that I deem impossible, like the drying up of the ocean.

sanskrit: abhiprāyaṃ tu jānāmi rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ sītāṃ prati mahābāho na ca ghātaṃ kariṣyati
english: "I know the intention of the evil-souled Rāvaṇa regarding Sītā, O mighty-armed one — he will not bring about her killing.

sanskrit: yācyamānaḥ subahuśo mayā hitacikīrṣuṇā vaidehīm utsṛjasveti na ca tat kṛtavān vacaḥ
english: "Though implored again and again by me, who sought his welfare, saying 'Release the princess of Videha,' he did not heed that counsel.

sanskrit: naiva sāmnā na bhedena na dānena kuto yudhā sā draṣṭum api śakyeta naiva cānyena kena cit
english: "She cannot be seen by conciliation, nor by sowing dissension, nor by bribery — far less by force of arms, nor by any other means whatsoever.

sanskrit: vānarān mohayitvā tu pratiyātaḥ sa rākṣasaḥ caityaṃ nikumbhilāṃ nāma yatra homaṃ kariṣyati
english: "That rākṣasa, having deluded the monkeys, has returned to the shrine called Nikumbhilā, where he will perform his oblation.

sanskrit: hutavān upayāto hi devair api savāsavaiḥ durādharṣo bhavaty eṣa saṃgrāme rāvaṇātmajaḥ
english: "For if he completes the oblation, this son of Rāvaṇa becomes invincible in battle even by the gods together with Vāsava.

sanskrit: tena mohayatā nūnam eṣā māyā prayojitā vighnam anvicchatā tāta vānarāṇāṃ parākrame sasainyās tatra gacchāmo yāvat tan na samāpyate
english: "Surely this illusion was deployed by him — ever seeking to obstruct — to confound the valour of the monkeys, dear one. Let us go there with our armies before it is completed."

sanskrit: tyajemaṃ naraśārdūlamithyā saṃtāpam āgatam sīdate hi balaṃ sarvaṃ dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ śokakarśitam
english: "Abandon, O tiger among men, this false anguish that has come upon you — for all the army is being crushed, seeing you wasted away by grief.

sanskrit: iha tvaṃ svastha hṛdayas tiṣṭha sattvasamucchritaḥ lakṣmaṇaṃ preṣayāsmābhiḥ saha sainyānukarṣibhiḥ
english: "Stay here with a serene heart, raised up in spirit; send Lakṣmaṇa with us who will draw the armies along.

sanskrit: eṣa taṃ naraśārdūlo rāvaṇiṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ tyājayiṣyati tat karma tato vadhyo bhaviṣyati
english: "This tiger among men will, with sharp arrows, cause Rāvaṇa's son to abandon his rite — and thereafter he will be fit to be slain.

sanskrit: tasyaite niśitās tīkṣṇāḥ patripatrāṅgavājinaḥ patatriṇa ivāsaumyāḥ śarāḥ pāsyanti śoṇitam
english: "His arrows, sharpened and keen, with feathers of wings, shafts of reeds, and horse-like fleetness, terrible as flying birds, shall drink blood.

sanskrit: tat saṃdiśa mahābāho lakṣmaṇaṃ śubhalakṣaṇam rākṣasasya vināśāya vajraṃ vajradharo yathā
english: "Therefore, O mighty-armed one, dispatch Lakṣmaṇa of auspicious marks for the destruction of that rākṣasa, as the thunderbolt-wielder hurls his thunderbolt.

sanskrit: manujavara na kālaviprakarṣo ripunidhanaṃ prati yat kṣamo 'dya kartum tvam atisṛja ripor vadhāya bāṇīm asurapuronmathane yathā mahendraḥ
english: "O foremost of men, there is no delay of the right moment when the slaying of the enemy is within reach — what you are able to do today, release the arrow-flight for the enemy's destruction, as great Indra smashed the demon's citadel."

sanskrit: samāptakarmā hi sa rākṣasendro bhavaty adṛśyaḥ samare surāsuraiḥ yuyutsatā tena samāptakarmaṇā bhavet surāṇām api saṃśayo mahān
english: "For when that lord of rākṣasas completes his rite he becomes invisible in battle even to gods and demons; if one were to fight with him after he has completed the rite, there would be great uncertainty even for the gods."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rāghavaḥ śokakarśitaḥ nopadhārayate vyaktaṃ yad uktaṃ tena rakṣasā
english: Hearing those words of his, Rāghava, wasted by grief, did not clearly comprehend what had been said by that rākṣasa.

sanskrit: tato dhairyam avaṣṭabhya rāmaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ vibhīṣaṇam upāsīnam uvāca kapisaṃnidhau
english: Then Rāma, conqueror of enemy cities, steadying himself with composure, spoke to Vibhīṣaṇa who sat beside him, in the presence of the monkeys:

sanskrit: nairṛtādhipate vākyaṃ yad uktaṃ te vibhīṣaṇa bhūyas tac chrotum icchāmi brūhi yat te vivakṣitam
english: "O lord of the Nairṛtas, Vibhīṣaṇa, what you have said — I wish to hear it again; speak what you intend to say."

sanskrit: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ yat tat punar idaṃ vākyaṃ babhāṣe sa vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Hearing Rāghava's words, Vibhīṣaṇa, skilled in speech, once more spoke these words:

sanskrit: yathājñaptaṃ mahābāho tvayā gulmaniveśanam tat tathānuṣṭhitaṃ vīra tvadvākyasamanantaram
english: "O mighty-armed one, the stationing of the outposts as commanded by you, O hero, was carried out immediately after your order.

sanskrit: tāny anīkāni sarvāṇi vibhaktāni samantataḥ vinyastā yūthapāś caiva yathānyāyaṃ vibhāgaśaḥ
english: "All those divisions have been deployed on all sides, and the troop-commanders have been posted in proper order according to their assigned positions.

sanskrit: bhūyas tu mama vijāpyaṃ tac chṛṇuṣva mahāyaśaḥ tvayy akāraṇasaṃtapte saṃtaptahṛdayā vayam
english: "But there is something more I must report — hear it, O greatly renowned one: with you tormented without cause, we are tormented in our hearts.

sanskrit: tyaja rājann imaṃ śokaṃ mithyā saṃtāpam āgatam tad iyaṃ tyajyatāṃ cintā śatruharṣavivardhanī
english: "Abandon, O king, this sorrow, this false anguish that has come upon you — let this anxiety be cast off, for it increases the enemy's joy.

sanskrit: udyamaḥ kriyatāṃ vīra harṣaḥ samupasevyatām prāptavyā yadi te sītā hantavyaś ca niśācarāḥ
english: "Let effort be made, O hero; let courage be cultivated — if Sītā is to be regained and the night-wanderers are to be slain.

sanskrit: raghunandana vakṣyāmi śrūyatāṃ me hitaṃ vacaḥ sādhv ayaṃ yātu saumitrir balena mahatā vṛtaḥ nikumbhilāyāṃ saṃprāpya hantuṃ rāvaṇim āhave
english: "O joy of the Raghus, I shall speak — hear my beneficial words: let Saumitri go, attended by a great army, to Nikumbhilā, to slay Rāvaṇa's son in battle.

sanskrit: dhanurmaṇḍalanirmuktair āśīviṣaviṣopamaiḥ śarair hantuṃ maheṣvāso rāvaṇiṃ samitiṃjayaḥ
english: "That great archer, victor in battle, to slay Rāvaṇa's son with arrows released from the arc of the bow, venomous as the poison of a serpent.

sanskrit: tena vīreṇa tapasā varadānāt svayambhutaḥ astraṃ brahmaśiraḥ prāptaṃ kāmagāś ca turaṃgamāḥ
english: "By that hero through his austerities and by boon from the Self-born, the Brahmaśiras weapon was obtained, as well as horses that go wherever desired.

sanskrit: nikumbhilām asaṃprāptam ahutāgniṃ ca yo ripuḥ tvām ātatāyinaṃ hanyād indraśatro sa te vadhaḥ ity evaṃ vihito rājan vadhas tasyaiva dhīmataḥ
english: "'The enemy who slays you, O enemy of Indra, before you have reached Nikumbhilā and before you have offered into the fire — that is your death' — thus, O king, the death of that wise one has been ordained.

sanskrit: vadhāyendrajito rāma taṃ diśasva mahābalam hate tasmin hataṃ viddhi rāvaṇaṃ sasuhṛjjanam
english: "O Rāma, dispatch that mighty one for the slaying of Indrajit; with him slain, know that Rāvaṇa is slain together with his kinsmen."

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇavacaḥ śrutva rāmo vākyam athābravīt jānāmi tasya raudrasya māyāṃ satyaparākrama
english: Having heard Vibhīṣaṇa's words, Rāma then spoke: "I know the illusion of that terrible one, O you whose valour is truth.

sanskrit: sa hi brahmāstravit prājño mahāmāyo mahābalaḥ karoty asaṃjñān saṃgrāme devān savaruṇān api
english: "He is skilled in the Brahma-weapon, wise, a great master of illusion, of great strength — in battle he renders even the gods together with Varuṇa unconscious.

sanskrit: tasyāntarikṣe carato rathasthasya mahāyaśaḥ na gatir jñāyate vīrasūryasyevābhrasaṃplave
english: "Of him moving through the sky in his chariot, O greatly renowned one, the course is not known, as the sun's course is unknown in a confluence of clouds.

sanskrit: rāghavas tu ripor jñātvā māyāvīryaṃ durātmanaḥ lakṣmaṇaṃ kīrtisaṃpannam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: But Rāghava, having understood the illusory power of that evil-souled enemy, spoke these words to Lakṣmaṇa endowed with glory:

sanskrit: yad vānarendrasya balaṃ tena sarveṇa saṃvṛtaḥ hanūmatpramukhaiś caiva yūthapaiḥ sahalakṣmaṇa
english: "Surrounded by all of the monkey-king's forces, together with the troop-commanders headed by Hanumān, O Lakṣmaṇa,

sanskrit: jāmbavenarkṣapatinā saha sainyena saṃvṛtaḥ jahi taṃ rākṣasasutaṃ māyābalaviśāradam
english: "surrounded by the army together with Jāmbavān, the lord of bears — slay that son of the rākṣasa, skilled in the power of illusion.

sanskrit: ayaṃ tvāṃ sacivaiḥ sārdhaṃ mahātmā rajanīcaraḥ abhijñas tasya deśasya pṛṣṭhato 'nugamiṣyati
english: "This great-souled night-wanderer, who knows that terrain, will follow at your back together with his counsellors."

sanskrit: rāghavasya vacaḥ śrutvā lakṣmaṇaḥ savibhīṣaṇaḥ jagrāha kārmukaṃ śreṣṭham anyad bhīmaparākramaḥ
english: Hearing Rāghava's words, Lakṣmaṇa of fierce valour, together with Vibhīṣaṇa, took up another supreme bow.

sanskrit: saṃnaddhaḥ kavacī khaḍgī sa śarī hemacāpadhṛk rāmapādāv upaspṛśya hṛṣṭaḥ saumitrir abravīt
english: Girded, clad in armour, bearing a sword, equipped with arrows, holding a golden bow, Saumitri touched Rāma's feet and spoke with delight:

sanskrit: adya matkārmukonmukhāḥ śarā nirbhidya rāvaṇim laṅkām abhipatiṣyanti haṃsāḥ puṣkariṇīm iva
english: "Today arrows loosed from my bow, piercing through Rāvaṇa's son, shall swoop upon Laṅkā as geese swoop upon a lotus-lake.

sanskrit: adyaiva tasya raudrasya śarīraṃ māmakāḥ śarāḥ vidhamiṣyanti hatvā taṃ mahācāpaguṇacyutāḥ
english: "This very day my arrows, released from the string of the great bow and slaying that terrible one, shall scatter his body."

sanskrit: sa evam uktvā dyutimān vacanaṃ bhrātur agrataḥ sa rāvaṇivadhākāṅkṣī lakṣmaṇas tvarito yayau
english: Having thus spoken these words before his glorious brother, Lakṣmaṇa, eager for the slaying of Rāvaṇa's son, departed swiftly.

sanskrit: so 'bhivādya guroḥ pādau kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam nikumbhilām abhiyayau caityaṃ rāvaṇipālitam
english: Having paid reverence to his elder's feet and circumambulated him, he marched to Nikumbhilā, the shrine guarded by Rāvaṇa's son.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇena sahito rājaputraḥ pratāpavān kṛtasvastyayano bhrātrā lakṣmaṇas tvarito yayau
english: The royal prince Lakṣmaṇa of great majesty, accompanied by Vibhīṣaṇa, having received his brother's blessing, went forth swiftly.

sanskrit: vānarāṇāṃ sahasrais tu hanūmān bahubhir vṛtaḥ vibhīṣaṇaḥ sahāmātyas tadā lakṣmaṇam anvagāt
english: Hanumān, surrounded by many thousands of monkeys, and Vibhīṣaṇa with his ministers, then followed after Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: mahatā harisainyena savegam abhisaṃvṛtaḥ ṛkṣarājabalaṃ caiva dadarśa pathi viṣṭhitam
english: Swiftly surrounded by the great monkey-army, he also beheld on the road the forces of the king of bears standing arrayed.

sanskrit: sa gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ saumitrir mitranandanaḥ rākṣasendrabalaṃ dūrād apaśyad vyūham āsthitam
english: Saumitri, delight of his friend, having traversed a great distance of road, saw from afar the army of the rākṣasa-lord drawn up in battle array.

sanskrit: sa saṃprāpya dhanuṣpāṇir māyāyogam ariṃdama tasthau brahmavidhānena vijetuṃ raghunandanaḥ
english: He, bow in hand, arriving at the site of the illusion-rite, O subduer of foes, stood firm in accordance with the Brahman procedure, in order to conquer — that joy of the Raghu line.

sanskrit: vividham amalaśastrabhāsvaraṃ tad dhvajagahanaṃ vipulaṃ mahārathaiś ca pratibhayatamam aprameyavegaṃ timiram iva dviṣatāṃ balaṃ viveśa
english: He entered that army of enemies — blazing with the radiance of diverse immaculate weapons, dense with banners, vast with great charioteers, most terrifying, of immeasurable speed — like darkness.
